panels.title: THE ARCHIVE OPENS
panels.action_beat: Raven opens the giant old book on the desk in his tower archive. The cover turns and the camera enters the page, revealing the salary jar on Rex’s office desk.
panels.voiceover_text: What if today your paycheck came in beer?
panels.on_screen_gag: The pay packet becomes a jar as the page opens.
panels.because: Raven opens the book to test an imagined present-day paycheck under an ancient ration system.
panels.outcome: The opened page reveals Rex preparing the beer salary.

panels.title: LIQUID SALARY
panels.era_setting: Present-day office/ATM imagined with Late Uruk costume accents; not a historical reconstruction
panels.action_beat: Rex, in a deliberately imagined modern office with Late Uruk wardrobe accents, pushes a large beer jar across the desk into Pip’s arms. Pip catches it with both hands while Rex maintains his false grin.
panels.voiceover_text: Rex pays Pip in warm beer.
panels.on_screen_gag: PAYDAY: LIQUID SALARY, drawn later by the program.
panels.because: The book’s paycheck question becomes a physical salary handoff.
panels.outcome: Pip now holds his entire imagined salary as a jar.

panels.title: BOTH HANDS REQUIRED
panels.era_setting: Present-day office/ATM imagined with Late Uruk costume accents; not a historical reconstruction
panels.action_beat: Pip tries to reach his jacket pocket for his wallet while holding the giant jar. Both hands must return to the jar before it slips; he remains safely upright. Rex watches without helping.
panels.voiceover_text: Pip’s salary now requires both hands.
panels.on_screen_gag: Pip cannot reach his wallet because his wage occupies both hands.
panels.because: The bulky jar delivered by Rex makes normal money handling impossible.
panels.outcome: Pip cannot use his wallet while carrying the jar.

panels.title: RENT IS STILL DUE
panels.era_setting: Present-day office/ATM imagined with Late Uruk costume accents; not a historical reconstruction
panels.action_beat: Mia holds up a blank rent notice, with its short editorial label added later. A modern landlord silhouette accepts a coin purse and refuses Pip’s offered jar; Mia raises an eyebrow.
panels.voiceover_text: Mia checks the rent. The landlord prefers money.
panels.on_screen_gag: RENT DUE overlay; the imagined modern landlord pushes the jar back.
panels.because: Pip’s inaccessible wallet brings Mia to the bill that actually needs payment.
panels.outcome: The imagined landlord rejects the beer jar as rent.

panels.title: TERRIBLE SAVINGS
panels.era_setting: Present-day office/ATM imagined with Late Uruk costume accents; not a historical reconstruction
panels.action_beat: Mia tilts the rejected jar toward Pip, frowns at its imagined warmth and points at his empty savings purse. Pip looks from the jar to the purse; no expiry number or clock appears.
panels.voiceover_text: Mia eyes the warm jar. Terrible savings account.
panels.on_screen_gag: The savings purse is empty while both hands hold the wage.
panels.because: The rent rejection forces Mia to ask whether this salary works as modern savings.
panels.outcome: Mia demands the real evidence behind the beer-pay premise.

panels.title: CHECK THE RECORD
panels.era_setting: Verified Late Uruk artifact, ca. 3100–3000 BCE
panels.action_beat: The actual licensed photograph of British Museum tablet ME 140855 fills the screen. A separate program-drawn box highlights the ration record. Raven’s PiP is hidden; no new inscription is invented.
panels.voiceover_text: The British Museum has a real beer-ration record.
panels.on_screen_gag: The official-looking office paperwork is replaced by a real clay record.
panels.because: Mia’s objection sends the narration to the surviving record rather than an invented expiry claim.
panels.outcome: The real tablet is now visible as evidence of beer rations.

panels.title: RATIONS, NOT PAYROLL
panels.era_setting: Verified Late Uruk artifact, ca. 3100–3000 BCE
panels.action_beat: On a second crop of the same real photograph, a program-drawn highlight isolates a documented beer-jar sign. A short caption reads BEER RATIONS outside the artifact; Raven remains hidden.
panels.voiceover_text: Workers received beer rations. Not a modern paycheck.
panels.on_screen_gag: One modern payroll analogy meets a specific ancient ration record.
panels.because: The real tablet lets the narrator distinguish recorded rations from a modern cash wage.
panels.outcome: The distinction between ration evidence and a modern paycheck is established.

panels.title: REX FINDS A LOOPHOLE
panels.era_setting: Present-day office/ATM imagined with Late Uruk costume accents; not a historical reconstruction
panels.action_beat: Back in the explicitly imagined office, Pip reads a reproduction displayed without invented writing. Rex peers over his shoulder, spots the ration idea and gestures triumphantly toward the remaining jars.
panels.voiceover_text: Pip reads the record. Rex spots a loophole.
panels.on_screen_gag: Rex treats the modern analogy as an excuse to supply even more jars.
panels.because: The ration evidence becomes Rex’s fictional managerial excuse to expand liquid payroll.
panels.outcome: Rex calls for an increase in jar-based payroll.

panels.title: ENTER TIMMY
panels.era_setting: Present-day office/ATM imagined with Late Uruk costume accents; not a historical reconstruction
panels.action_beat: Timmy eagerly raises his hand and rolls a small handcart toward Rex’s jar shelf. Rex points him toward the jars. Timmy does not drink and handles only a safe manageable load.
panels.on_screen_gag: An eager apprentice takes a terrible management idea literally.
panels.because: Rex’s request gives Timmy a chance to take the system to an absurd extreme.
panels.outcome: Timmy starts moving a handcart of empty sealed jars into the office.

panels.title: ZERO DESK SPACE
panels.era_setting: Present-day office/ATM imagined with Late Uruk costume accents; not a historical reconstruction
panels.action_beat: Timmy brings the handcart piled with empty sealed jars to Pip’s desk and arranges them over every work surface. Pip tries to open a ledger but the jars occupy its space.
panels.voiceover_text: More jars. Less desk. No actual work.
panels.on_screen_gag: Jars occupy every place where work could happen.
panels.because: Timmy’s literal payroll improvement fills the office with jars instead of usable wages.
panels.outcome: Jars block Pip’s work surface and the ledger stays closed.

panels.title: REX COUNTS SUCCESS
panels.era_setting: Present-day office/ATM imagined with Late Uruk costume accents; not a historical reconstruction
panels.action_beat: Rex counts the jars with an exaggerated satisfied grin while Pip, blocked by the pile, holds a closed work ledger. Timmy proudly presents the useless stack.
panels.voiceover_text: Rex counts the jars as productivity.
panels.on_screen_gag: Rex celebrates the count while no work happens.
panels.because: Blocked work does not stop Rex from treating the jar pile as a success metric.
panels.outcome: The office is full of jars but the rent remains unpaid.

panels.title: FIND A DEPOSIT SLOT
panels.era_setting: Present-day office/ATM imagined with Late Uruk costume accents; not a historical reconstruction
panels.action_beat: Mia taps the still-unpaid rent notice and points toward an obviously modern cash machine at the office entrance. Pip lifts one manageable jar and heads toward it.
panels.voiceover_text: Mia points to rent. Pip finds a cash machine.
panels.on_screen_gag: The unpaid bill sends the liquid wage to an unsuitable modern machine.
panels.because: Rex’s jar count leaves the original rent problem unresolved.
panels.outcome: Pip approaches a modern cash machine carrying his beer salary.

panels.title: DEPOSIT DECLINED
panels.era_setting: Present-day office/ATM imagined with Late Uruk costume accents; not a historical reconstruction
panels.action_beat: Pip gently tilts the jar toward the cash machine’s banknote slot. A small spill runs down the exterior; the machine’s closed slot refuses it. Mia watches with stunned disbelief. No generated lettering appears.
panels.voiceover_text: He tries depositing his salary. The slot declines.
panels.on_screen_gag: NO LIQUID DEPOSITS label is drawn later; the spill stays outside the machine.
panels.because: Pip tries the only modern banking tool available to solve the rent problem.
panels.outcome: The cash machine refuses liquid wages.

panels.title: LIQUID ASSETS
panels.era_setting: Present-day office/ATM imagined with Late Uruk costume accents; not a historical reconstruction
panels.action_beat: Pip stops pouring and stares at the refused deposit slot while holding the nearly upright jar. The modern machine remains closed and Mia slowly turns toward him.
panels.on_screen_gag: The liquid-assets phrase resolves literally at the closed banknote slot.
panels.because: The rejected deposit turns the salary metaphor into a visible physical punchline.
panels.outcome: Mia has seen enough of the failed liquid deposit.

panels.title: DUAL FACEPALM
panels.era_setting: Present-day office/ATM imagined with Late Uruk costume accents; not a historical reconstruction
panels.action_beat: Mia covers her forehead with one hand beside the refused cash machine. A small separate Raven PiP performs his registered facepalm. Rex slides another jar toward Pip, maintaining the same false smile.
panels.on_screen_gag: Rex offers another jar as the imagined overdraft.
panels.because: The failed deposit makes Mia and Raven react while Rex doubles down on his own rule.
panels.outcome: The absurd experiment ends and Raven turns to its real source record.

panels.title: THE ARCHIVE RECEIPT
panels.action_beat: A clean program-drawn archive card shows the verified British Museum reference, its date and object identifiers. Raven appears as a small smug presenter; all bibliographic text is a separate graphic layer.
panels.voiceover_text: Of course. There’s paperwork. Full sources below.
panels.on_screen_gag: The imaginary payroll disaster ends with an actual documentary receipt.
panels.because: Raven closes the experiment by showing exactly which record supports the historical premise.
panels.outcome: The viewer receives the verified citation and the full-source link.
